# Repository catalog

Every repository that builds, specifies, verifies or operates the platform, with one purpose each and the disposition decided in PDR-0002. A repository exists only when it meets an admission criterion and owns at least one seam; anything else is a directory in an existing repository.

## Admission criteria

- **C1** Runs in a distinct trust domain or as a distinct security principal.
- **C2** Released on its own cadence behind a versioned contract registered as a seam.
- **C3** Separation of duties (for example an independent reviewer merges).
- **C4** Needs different visibility or licensing (private fleet state, public spec).

## Product definition

### agent-bot-platform

Criteria: C3, C4.

Owns: Vision, scope, requirements (R, QA) and traceability; Architecture, trust domains, repository catalog and seams; Platform decision records (PDR) and the cross-repo ADR index; Security, privacy, intelligence and verification strategy; Release criteria, stage gates, roadmap, risks, drift register; Frozen source papers (S, X).

Must not own: Machine-readable schemas, fixtures, error codes (soul-contracts); Executable tests (soul-conformance); Implementation specs and repo-local ADRs (component repos); Engineering process and SOPs (qwts/qwts-agent-sop).

## Contracts and verification

### soul-contracts

Criteria: C2, C4; work packages: WP1.

Owns: JSON Schemas per contract family (hq/v1, task/v1, wire/v1, ...); Canonicalization vectors and positive/negative fixtures; Error registry (codes added here before any implementation emits them).

Must not own: Requirement wording, glossary, traceability matrix, papers (move to the platform under PDR-0001).

### soul-conformance

Criteria: C3; work packages: WP7.

Owns: T01-T30 suites, hostile-member suite, simulators, hello.soul; Eval harness and release conformance reports.

Must not own: What a test must prove (registry/tests.yaml in the platform).

## Host and remote services

### agent-bot

Criteria: C1; trust domain: Owner-operated remote service; trusted for credential custody and issuance only; work packages: WP2.

Owns: Key custody, enrollment, device-bound short-lived credential minting, issuance records; Catalog signing key and admin catalog publish; Web console and its MCP tools.

Must not own: Lifecycle or any control path to a host (R2).

Follow-up: Take over the scope of agent-github-identity (archived 2026-11-07), evaluating its durable write receipts for the GitHub write tools.

### agent-bot-daemon

Criteria: C1; trust domain: Trusted local host service, outside every Soul; work packages: WP2, WP4, WP6.

Owns: hq/v1 owner and member API, admission, grants, leases, epochs; Action ledger, task authority, budgets, reconciliation, approvals; Plugin host for identity, comms and soul-runtime plugins; HQ CLI; Device key and short-lived credentials held in memory.

Must not own: Long-lived signing keys (identity service); Host-side credentials at rest and policy writes (agent-bot-machine admin sandbox); Wire framing or task state library code (agent-comms).

Follow-up: Move platform-level sections of docs/daemon-plugin-split.md (architecture, decisions D1-D4) into the platform; add AGENTS.md with the governed block.

### agent-bot-machine

Criteria: C1; trust domain: Host admin account sandbox (brew admin, never root).

Owns: Self-tapped Homebrew formula, machine bootstrap, catalog installs; Host-side credentials and signed policy in the admin sandbox (agent-bot-daemon D4); Owner-presence verification of Secure Enclave signatures (agent-bot-daemon D4); The signed local channel endpoint and signed receipts.

Must not own: HQ authority (S7 made it HQ; agent-bot-daemon D1 moved HQ to agent-bot-daemon, see DRIFT-002).

Follow-up: README still introduces it as managed-machine.

### managed-machine-config

Criteria: C4.

Owns: Dotfiles, catalog inputs, versioned fleet state; Linux and macOS member-isolation profiles (S7 section 3.10).

Must not own: Secrets or grants.

Follow-up: Transfer to true-line alongside agent-bot-machine.

### agent-comms

Criteria: C1, C2; trust domain: Broker mode runs inside HQ's trust domain; client mode inside the Soul (untrusted for authority); relay mode untrusted for content; work packages: WP4.

Owns: Wire framing, sealing profile, mailbox, outbox, deduplication store interface; Task state machine library (decides nothing about authority); Relay mode, A2A and MCP gateways.

Must not own: Authority decisions or keys (HQ); authoritative task state (HQ's store).

Follow-up: Transfer to true-line; load soul-contracts fixtures; reconcile its wire and task docs (DRIFT-004).

## Inside the Soul

### agent-bot-identity

Criteria: C2; trust domain: Inside the Soul; untrusted for authority; work packages: WP3.

Owns: agent-bot CLI, git and harness hooks, fail-closed gh; GitHub App attribution and commit trailers.

Must not own: HQ authority, keyd, approvals, census (move to agent-bot-daemon per agent-bot-identity ADR-1183); Soul runtime entry point (move to the Soul runtime repo).

Follow-up: Transfer to true-line; supersede agent-bot-identity ADR-0332 (DRIFT-003); retire docs/identity-contract.md in favor of the platform glossary.

### agent-bot-souls

Criteria: C2; trust domain: Inside the Soul; untrusted for authority; work packages: WP3, WP5.

Owns: agent-bot soul run / soul chat, ACP server and client; Member supervision, cooperative scheduling, recovery ladder; Typed notes, dream runs and candidate staging.

Must not own: Keys or grant decisions.

### soul-package

Criteria: C1, C2; work packages: WP5.

Owns: Package layout and data classes (S4), manifest digests; Import validation that HQ runs before any untrusted execution (T16); soul build renderer and the render-plugin API.

Must not own: Runtime behavior of a Soul.

### soul-adapters

Criteria: C2; work packages: WP3.

Owns: One package per harness, each with a signed qualification.json per version.

Must not own: Dependencies on runtime internals (contracts and soul-package only).

Follow-up: Move the harness-adapter contract into soul-contracts so the seam is versioned rather than repo-local.

## Owner products (proprietary, on top of the platform)

### geniusbar

Criteria: C1, C4; trust domain: Owner's authenticated session on the host; enforces nothing; work packages: WP6.

Owns: Menubar UI, enrollment flow, approval and receipt views.

Must not own: Any authority; it is a client of HQ only.

Follow-up: Switch backend from the agent-bot daemon to hq/v1. GeniusBar is a code name only (owner, 2026-11-07); choose a product name before any public release (DRIFT-006, RISK-010). Proprietary, outside the MIT platform.

## Repositories to merge, archive or leave outside the product

| Repository | Disposition | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| agent-machine-configurations | Archive | Duplicates managed-machine-config's purpose with no content. |
| agent-github-identity | Merge into agent-bot | Third home for GitHub App identity (with agent-bot and agent-bot-identity). The identity service already holds the App keys and serves MCP tools. |
| agent-watchtower | Keep | Owner direction 2026-11-07: a standalone security product, not part of the platform. It consumes hq/v1 read-only and cannot be a second HQ. |
| embedded-skills | Adjacent, outside the product | Candidate delivery mechanism for Soul primitives; record the seam before the runtime depends on it. |
| agent-fleet | Adjacent, outside the product | Overlaps agent-bot-machine fleet enrollment and qwts-agent-inventory; fold into agent-bot-machine when HQ diagnostics exist. |
| agent-space | Adjacent, outside the product | Superseded by Soul transfer and backup (S4, soul-package) once those exist. |
| engineering-relay | Adjacent, outside the product | Process layer. Overlaps the SDLC guides in qwts-agent-sop (DRIFT-008); the platform links to one process source only. |
